$comment: Provenance for every picture this repository SHIPS for a kind of break. The rule is the
one assets/pads/MANIFEST.json states and it is not relaxed for images: CC0 or an equivalent
public-domain dedication, and attribution-requiring work is refused rather than credited,
because a radio station has nowhere to put a credit and the obligation would travel to the
operator in silence.
Both entries below answer that rule the cleanest way there is: they were DRAWN for this
repository rather than sourced, so there is nobody to credit and nothing to verify. Each one
composites the station's OWN mark -- the skull from apps/ios's app icon, which is the largest
copy in the tree and the only one with no lettering -- into the glyph rather than beside it:
the skull is what is inside the cloud, and what is in the photograph on the front page.
The `.svg` each was drawn as sits beside the `.png` so the next person can edit the artwork
instead of tracing it, and it references the mark by path rather than embedding it, so the
source stays a few kilobytes. The PNG is what ships, because a hardware player fetches a
picture and will not render SVG; each was rasterised with the command the SVG names.
`sha256` is of the PNG, and it is what makes an entry checkable by somebody who was not
here. `kind` is `segments.kind`, which is what decides which break wears which file: a new
kind is a file named after it plus a line here, and nothing in the code learns its name.
These are DEFAULTS. The station writes each one into its own art store on first boot and
serves it from there; an operator who uploads their own replaces the bytes under the same
id, and reverting re-reads the file named here. Nothing under `/data` or `/media` is a copy
of this directory -- it is part of the image, so an upgrade that improves a picture is what
a revert then restores.
